questions.lead: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa in oil on a white poplar panel, probably between 1503 and 1506, and may have kept working on it as late as 1517. Today the portrait hangs in the Louvre in Paris.
questions.prompt: Who acquired the Mona Lisa after Leonardo's death in 1519?

questions.lead: The piano was invented in Italy: an inventory drawn up by the Medici family shows that one existed by 1700. The credit goes to the keeper of the instruments for Ferdinando de' Medici, Grand Prince of Tuscany, a man from Padua.
questions.prompt: Who is credited with inventing the piano?

questions.lead: Most modern pianos have 88 keys, spanning seven octaves plus a minor third, from A0 to C8. They are laid out in a repeating pattern of white and black keys.
questions.prompt: How many black keys does a modern piano have?

questions.lead: King Francis I of France acquired the Mona Lisa after Leonardo's death in 1519, and it later became the property of the French Republic. It has been on display in the Louvre in Paris for more than two centuries.
questions.prompt: Since which year has the Mona Lisa normally been on display at the Louvre?

questions.lead: The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna in Agra, its tomb crowned by a marble dome 23 metres high. The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan had it built to house the tomb of his late wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
questions.prompt: The Taj Mahal was commissioned in 1631. In which year was the mausoleum completed?

explanations: King Francis I of France acquired the Mona Lisa after Leonardo's death in 1519. Leonardo had been working on the portrait since around 1503 and may have continued until as late as 1517.
Bartolomeo Cristofori of Padua, keeper of the instruments for Ferdinando de' Medici, is credited with inventing the piano. An inventory made by the Medici family shows that a piano existed by 1700.
Most modern pianos have 36 black keys alongside 52 white ones, making 88 in all. Together they span seven octaves plus a minor third, from A0 to C8.
The Mona Lisa has normally been on display at the Louvre in Paris since 1797. By then it had passed from the French kings into the property of the French Republic.
The mausoleum was completed in 1648, seventeen years after Shah Jahan commissioned it. Work on other parts of the complex went on for another five years.

sources.excerpt: It is painted in oil on a white poplar panel. It was believed to have been painted between 1503 and 1506; however, Leonardo may have continued working on it as late as 1517. King Francis I of France acquired the Mona Lisa after Leonardo's death in 1519, and it became the property of the French Republic. It has normally been on display at the Louvre in Paris since 1797.

Most modern pianos have 52 white keys and 36 black keys, for a total of 88 keys (seven octaves plus a minor third, from A0 to C8). The invention of the piano is credited to Bartolomeo Cristofori of Padua, Italy, who was employed by Ferdinando de' Medici, Grand Prince of Tuscany, as the Keeper of the Instruments. An inventory made by his employers, the Medici family, indicates the existence of a piano by 1700.

It was commissioned in 1631 by the fifth Mughal emperor, Shah Jahan (r. 1628–1658), to house the tomb of his late wife, Mumtaz Mahal; it also houses the tomb of Shah Jahan himself. Construction of the mausoleum was completed in 1648, although work on other parts of the complex continued for another five years. The predominant feature of the mausoleum is the 23-metre (75 ft) high marble dome that surmounts the tomb.
